name: Vegan Grocery Checklist
description: A plant-based shopping list organized by category, from produce and legumes to whole grains, plant milks and nuts.

items.text: Berries, apples, bananas and seasonal fruit

items.note: Aim for a wide range of colors for varied nutrients.

items.text: Dried or low-sodium canned beans (black, kidney, cannellini)

items.note: Include a protein source at most meals.
Whole grains add fiber and pair well with legumes.

items.text: Unsweetened soy, oat or almond milk

items.note: Fortified options help replace dairy calcium.
Flax, chia and walnuts provide plant omega-3s.

items.text: Nutritional yeast for a cheesy, B-vitamin boost
Vitamin B12 supplement or B12-fortified foods
items.note: B12 is essential on a vegan diet and not reliable from plants alone.

items.text: No-salt-added canned tomatoes and coconut milk
Important: this is general information, not nutritional or medical advice
items.note: For a balanced vegan diet and any supplements, consult a doctor or registered dietitian.

faq.a: A vegan diet excludes all animal products, including meat, fish, dairy, eggs and honey. It is built around vegetables, fruit, legumes, whole grains, nuts, seeds and plant-based alternatives. With a little planning it can cover your nutritional needs.

Plant protein comes from beans, lentils, chickpeas, tofu, tempeh, edamame, seitan, nuts, seeds and whole grains. Including a protein source at each meal and eating a variety of plants across the day helps you get enough.

faq.q: Do I need any supplements on a vegan diet?
faq.a: Vitamin B12 is the key one, since it is not reliably found in plant foods, so a supplement or fortified foods are recommended. Many people also consider vitamin D, omega-3 and iodine. Ask a doctor or dietitian about what is right for you.

faq.q: Can I print this vegan grocery checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF to take to the store, ticking off each plant-based staple by category as you shop.

No. This is general information, not medical or dietary advice. For a balanced vegan diet, especially for children, during pregnancy or with a health condition, consult your doctor or a registered dietitian.
